title.title: The generator problem for finite factors
title.subtitle: Claim: every II$_1$ factor with separable predual is generated by a single operator

beats.text: Start from an irreducible hyperfinite subfactor $P$ of a II$_1$ factor $M$
$P$ is singly generated, and two generators combine into one

achievement.label: Kadison's generator problem (1967)
statement: M = W^*(x) \text{ for every II}_1 \text{ factor with separable predual}
achievement.context: Before: type I, properly infinite, Cartan, property $\Gamma$ and many more; $L(\mathbb F_n)$ open
achievement.note: With the direct-integral reduction: every separable von Neumann algebra

verify.detail: Single generation and the relative dense-$G_\delta$ statement are both in Lean
verify.ourCheck: We checked it does not use family 287; we did not build the Lean

sources.quote: Kadison's generator problem (1967 Baton Rouge problem list)
I checked whether it quietly uses family 287; it does not.

plain: Can a whole infinite algebra of operators be built from just one operator? Like one key cutting every lock

steps: Find a well-understood piece inside the algebra (Popa)
Add a typical unitary: together they generate everything
That piece needs one generator, and two combine into one

voice.text: Inside the factor, take a well-understood hyperfinite piece P, then add a generic unitary u.
Together they generate everything; P needs one generator, and two combine into one.
Claimed: every such factor is singly generated.
